trial_allocation.allocation_rationale: Baseline model — fixed defaults, no HPO needed.
Random Forest is robust but has a moderate search space (n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_split). 15 trials are sufficient to find a strong configuration without overfitting on 24 features.

XGBoost has a large, complex search space (learning_rate, max_depth, subsample, colsample_bytree, reg_alpha, reg_lambda) and is highly sensitive to hyperparameters. 20 trials ensure adequate exploration to maximize ROC-AUC.
LightGBM is also complex but often converges faster than XGBoost due to its leaf-wise growth. 15 trials provide a good balance between exploration and compute time.
Extra Trees has low sensitivity to hyperparameters compared to boosting models, as it relies on random splits. 5 trials are enough to tune n_estimators and max_depth.
